truths.truth: risk-check run over a range whose DIFF BODY is empty writes a completed check - checked:true, inconclusive:false, matches:[], empty:true - decided from the body and not from base_id === head_id, while a diff read that FAILED still writes checked:false, inconclusive:true.
truths.evidence: cadence-core/bin/lib/risk-diff.mjs:321 (non-string body keeps checked:false, empty:false), :328 (string body that trims to nothing is checked:true, empty:true), :372 (empty:false on the scanned return, so ABSENCE marks a pre-split record); cadence-core/bin/planning.mjs:4043 (record) and :4057 (envelope) both carry scan.empty. Behaviour observed through the real CLI: `node --test cadence-core/bin/risk-diff.test.mjs` 74/74, naming `risk-check run: a SAME-COMMIT range is a completed empty check, not an unchecked one`, `risk-check run: a REVERT PAIR is empty too - the ids differ and the net diff does not` (asserts base_id !== head_id), and `risk-check run: an unreadable range is ok:false, and STILL leaves its record`. Mutation in a scratch copy (collapsing :328 back to checked:false, inconclusive:true, empty:false) reddens exactly 4 rows including both of the above; restored.

The mutation of truth 1 reddens exactly this row, so AC2's "reverting the run-side fix reddens the test" clause is observed, not asserted. `risk-check status: a PRE-FIX empty-range record still refuses - an absent flag is not empty` (:601-615) pins D-03 with state `unchecked` and reason `risk-record-missing`.

gaps.name: The phase's own round-1 risk_surface receipt cites the amended sha, so the phase-wide risk-check status refuses
gaps.reason: behavior wrong - the `rearm` receipt written for round 1 carries sha 95ba7b2 (the fix commit, later amended to f5efcb4 and now unreachable: `git merge-base --is-ancestor 95ba7b2 HEAD` -> NOT-ancestor) instead of the reviewed head 31c2085, so no receipt settles the first matched record.
gaps.evidence: .planning/trace.jsonl, corr 3-dc4c4b1: outcome/risk_check at 13:52:12 head_id 31c2085 matches ['destructive']; outcome/rearm at 13:58:33 sha 95ba7b2 base dc4c4b1; outcome/risk_check at 14:00:20 head_id f5efcb4 matches ['destructive']; outcome/gate_pass at 14:00:24 sha f5efcb4 base dc4c4b1 round 2. `node cadence-core/bin/planning.mjs risk-check status --phase 3` -> ok:false, reason risk-fire-missing, state unfired, missing ['1']. The per-plan spelling the workflow actually uses (execute.md:310, with --base/--head) returns ok:true, and no workflow, reference, skill or bin caller invokes the phase-wide arm, so nothing automated is blocked - the cost is an auditor reading the phase's gate history as unsettled. Related and already disclosed: .planning/phases/3/ADJUDICATION-risk_surface-plan-1.json:30 records `fix_commit: 95ba7b2` for the same reason.
gaps.missing: Either append a rearm/gate_pass receipt for the round-1 range (`--sha 31c2085 --base dc4c4b1 --trigger risk_surface --plan 1` under corr 3-dc4c4b1), or narrow SUMMARY's deviation wording to say the gate is ok:true under the per-plan spelling execute.md uses and that the phase-wide arm still reports risk-fire-missing on the round-1 record.

human_checks.name: Run /cad-execute <N> --rerun against a phase whose tasks are all already satisfied, and transcribe the outcome into .planning/phases/3/UAT.md item 3
human_checks.expected: The run reaches completion with no user override of a blocking gate: the risk-check run over the empty committed range answers checked:true, inconclusive:false, matches:[], empty:true, and the following `risk-check status --phase <N> --plan <k> --base {pre-plan HEAD} --head HEAD` returns ok:true with state `recorded` rather than refusing risk-record-missing.
human_checks.why_human: Out of reach, not merely unexercised: /cad-execute is a slash command dispatched into an interactive Claude Code session with a live coordinator and subagent spend, and the criterion is specifically that no HUMAN override was needed - which only a human sitting in that run can observe. The seam halves it rests on are already verified end to end here (truths 1 and 2, both driven through the real CLI), and D-11 records that the machine trace of the run is gitignored, so the transcription into UAT.md is the only durable record.
